topic: Hip fracture and registry data quality

audits.title: INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE ACCURACY OF UK NATIONAL HIP FRACTURE DATABASE INTRAOPERATIVE DATA: A CLOSED LOOP AUDIT WITH POSITIVE RESULTS
audits.standard: Completion of NHFD V13.0 theatre collection sheet by the operating surgeon >80%, with improved accuracy
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic unit, Craigavon Area Hospital (Southern Health and Social Care Trust)

cycle1.result: 56% (n=14) had a completed V13.0 form; of these 21% (n=3) were 100% accurate.

audits.intervention: Results presented with education on V13.0 at the monthly trust audit meeting, and a sticker added to the hip fracture pre-operative checklist (time of admission and reason for delay).

cycle2.result: 81% (n=25) had a completed form; accuracy increased to 56% (n=14).

audits.citation: Cunningham B, Donnell I, Patton S. INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE ACCURACY OF UK NATIONAL HIP FRACTURE DATABASE INTRAOPERATIVE DATA: A CLOSED LOOP AUDIT WITH POSITIVE RESULTS. Orthopaedic Proceedings. 2023;105-B(SUPP_9):34-34. doi:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.9.034.

audits.title: Data quality audit of the arthroplasty clinical outcomes registry NSW.
audits.standard: Benchmark of 95.0% for data completeness and accuracy against reabstracted medical record data
audits.setting: Arthroplasty Clinical Outcomes Registry NSW (ACORN); two major hospitals (A and B) in New South Wales

cycle1.period: Surgery in 2012/2013 (first six months of data submission)
cycle1.result: Completeness 99.0% (1259/1272) Hospital A and 99.3% (1589/1600) Hospital B; accuracy 94.0% (2159/2296) Hospital A and 96.1% (2444/2542) Hospital B. 57.1% (28/49) of variables met the 95% accuracy benchmark in A and 74.5% (38/51) in B. Registry captured 93.5% (660/706) of eligible patients.

audits.other_findings: Most accuracy discrepancies were in comorbidity (medical history) data, e.g. hypertension, hyperlipidaemia and GIT; only 10.2% (A) and 8.0% (B) of records were entirely error-free. 100 records were sampled; one from Hospital A was excluded.
audits.citation: Seagrave KG, Naylor J, Armstrong E, Leong KM, Descallar J, Harris IA. Data quality audit of the arthroplasty clinical outcomes registry NSW. BMC Health Serv Res. 2014;14:512. doi:10.1186/s12913-014-0512-6. PMID: 25410899.

audits.title: Implementing large-scale data quality validation in a national arthroplasty registry to improve compliance : the National Joint Registry data quality audit programme.
audits.standard: Compliance of NJR entries validated against each unit's Patient Administration System; target 95% or higher compliance
audits.setting: National Joint Registry (England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man, Guernsey); national data quality audit of all NHS and independent sector arthroplasty units

cycle1.result: Baseline average organisation-level compliance 92.64% (92.6%), with over 7,000 cases in provider data but missing from the NJR; 9.7% of revision hips missing vs 5.6% of primaries, and 9.8% of revision knees vs 5.1% of primaries.

audits.intervention: Annual bidirectional data quality audit cycle: statements of missing cases sent to units for retrospective entry, named data quality lead per unit, data completeness awards and tariff top-up targets, audit reports with action plans to CEOs and clinical leads, unit visits, communications and user guides, and a semi-automated upload platform from 2018.

cycle2.result: Baseline compliance rose year-on-year to 96.0% in 2018/19, reaching 97.9% overall after closure of the audit cycle; 76.4% of units achieved >95% compliance (61.5% of units achieved ≥95% on first run of the 2018/19 audit). 314 units completed the 2018/19 audit.

audits.other_findings: Intermediate unit-level baseline compliance was 91.78% (2015/16), 92.46% (2016/17) and 94.12% (2017/18), with missing cases falling from 11,285 to 8,670; a persistent gap remained between primary and revision procedures.
audits.citation: Boulton C, Harrison C, Wilton T, Armstrong R, Young E, Pegg D, et al.. Implementing large-scale data quality validation in a national arthroplasty registry to improve compliance : the National Joint Registry data quality audit programme. Bone Jt Open. 2022;3(9):716-725. doi:10.1302/2633-1462.39.bjo-2022-0051.r1. PMID: 36106695.

audits.title: Development of a New Knee Arthroscopy Operative Proforma Saving Thousands of British Pounds.
audits.standard: Correct ICD-10 and OPCS-4 coding of arthroscopic knee procedures from the operation note; proforma based on Royal College guidance for operation notes
audits.setting: Two centres of one trauma and orthopaedic service (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust / North Manchester General Hospital), knee arthroscopy day cases

cycle1.result: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.

audits.intervention: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.

cycle2.result: 2/37 (5%) cases coded incorrectly; £86,886 as coded versus £89,540 after correction, a loss of £2654.

audits.other_findings: Most coding errors came from vague documentation of preoperative diagnoses and additional procedures (e.g. extra meniscectomy or cartilage debridement). Uptake of the proforma was slow and some cases were excluded for incorrect use of the form.
audits.citation: Habib Z, Jain S, Rasool MU, Saha S. Development of a New Knee Arthroscopy Operative Proforma Saving Thousands of British Pounds. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e48476. doi:10.7759/cureus.48476. PMID: 38024083.

audits.title: The National Joint Registry Data Quality Audit of elbow arthroplasty.
audits.standard: Completeness of NJR elbow dataset against Hospital Episode Statistics, and accuracy of recorded components
audits.setting: NHS hospitals in England; national collaborative audit with BOTA

cycle1.result: Completeness 63%; radial head arthroplasty completeness 35%; accuracy 94%; 5539 unmatched and 448 inaccurate arthroplasties from 254 hospitals

audits.intervention: National collaborative audit through trainees: hospitals checked records, added missing arthroplasties and corrected inaccurate ones

cycle2.result: Completeness 83% (total elbow arthroplasty 93%); radial head arthroplasty completeness 70%; accuracy 98% after correcting 212 of 448

audits.other_findings: 82% of unmatched records were confirmed missing; radial head arthroplasties drove most of the gap.
audits.citation: Hamoodi Z, Shapiro J, Sayers A, Whitehouse MR, Watts AC, NJR DQA-Elbows Collaborators, et al.. The National Joint Registry Data Quality Audit of elbow arthroplasty. Bone Joint J. 2024;106-B(12):1461-1468. doi:10.1302/0301-620x.106b12.bjj-2023-1372.r1. PMID: 39618239.

audits.standard: Correct HRG coding based on comorbidity and complication index
audits.setting: NHS Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Foundation Trust, laparoscopic cholecystectomies

cycle1.result: 69.23% of procedures coded incorrectly; £72,232 lost potential tariff (£372.33 per cholecystectomy); commonest correct code GA10J (CCI 3 in 29%), commonest wrong code GA10K (presumed CCI 0).

audits.standard: Accurate and complete coding of gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures

cycle1.result: Staff unaware of the coding system; typed discharge summaries usually inadequate for coding; considerable variation in proportion of procedures coded.

audits.intervention: Changes made to improve accuracy and completeness of coding (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Follow-up study showed the changes were effective (no figures in abstract).

audits.title: Coding plastic surgery operations: an audit of performance using OPCS-4.
audits.setting: Plastic surgery theatres and coding office, Morriston Hospital, Swansea

cycle1.result: Coding office vs theatre staff overall accuracy 78% vs 43%; procedural codes 98% vs 42%; primary codes 62% vs 74%.

audits.intervention: Results discussed with all relevant staff

cycle2.result: Only significant improvement was in overall accuracy of coding office records; coders better than theatre staff for primary codes (76% vs 56%).

audits.other_findings: Theatre coding judged poor and recommended to stop; 1/3 to 1/4 of essential codes by coders were inaccurate.
audits.citation: Colville RJ, Laing JH, Murison MS. Coding plastic surgery operations: an audit of performance using OPCS-4. Br J Plast Surg. 2000;53(5):420-422. doi:10.1054/bjps.2000.3323. PMID: 10876282.

audits.title: Audit of clinical coding of major head and neck operations.
audits.standard: Correct OPCS procedure coding reflective of work undertaken
audits.setting: University Department of Head and Neck Surgery, Manchester Royal Infirmary (tertiary referral centre)

cycle1.result: 47 of 99 (47.4%) original procedure codes were incorrect (revised coding generated 146 codes); HRG unchanged in 19 of 34 cases (55.9%); six cases never coded, equating to a 15,300 pound loss.

audits.other_findings: The coding system was found complicated, ambiguous and inaccurate, resulting in lost remuneration.

audits.title: False-positive coding for acute myocardial infarction on hospital discharge records: chart audit results from a tertiary centre.
audits.standard: Documentation criteria for acute myocardial infarction (symptomatic, ECG and enzymatic elements) in charts coded ICD-9-CM AMI

cycle1.result: 43 (21%) false-positives (95% CI 15 to 26%), i.e. charts coded AMI where criteria were not met.

audits.other_findings: Physician diagnosis of AMI appeared on the face sheet in 30 of the false-positive cases; common causes were recent AMI with transfer or readmission for angiography, and presumed AMI later disproved.
audits.citation: van Walraven C, Wang B, Ugnat AM, Naylor CD. False-positive coding for acute myocardial infarction on hospital discharge records: chart audit results from a tertiary centre. Can J Cardiol. 1990;6(9):383-386. PMID: 2276072.

audits.setting: Otolaryngology admissions and day cases, Queen's Hospital, Romford
audits.intervention: Regular education supported by an audit programme.

cycle2.result: Primary diagnosis changed in 13% (420), primary procedure in 13% (417), at least one change in 44% (1420), HRG change in 16% (514); regrouped under HRG 3.5 the rate was 9%.
